absent: Locking, concurrency and ordering rules for perf events, callchains, auxiliary buffers and power operations are not shown.
Transition order, return value handling and failure recovery for device power phases are not shown.
Concrete behavior behind indirect dispatch, sysfs display, trace device recording and capability checks is not shown.
Layout and limits of branch entries, address filters, output handles and register snapshots beyond the fields shown are not shown.
Initialization, teardown and lifetime rules for performance units and power tracing controls are not shown.

findings.text: Guest perf queries report virtualization state, guest instruction address, Intel processor trace interrupt status and mediated interrupt handling. The enabled build forwards each query through a runtime patchable indirect call facility with two macro spellings for different configurations. The disabled build makes the state, address and Intel queries yield zero while mediated handling does nothing.

Callchain capture appends instruction addresses into a caller supplied entry with separate accounting for total entries and for context markers. The context variant enforces a global per stack context limit, sets a saturation flag and signals stop when exhausted. The plain variant enforces a per context stack bound and also stops once the saturation flag is set, otherwise it appends and reports success.
Perf security gate identifiers are fixed integers where open is zero and processor, kernel and tracepoint are one, two and three respectively.
Paranoia is determined by comparing a global paranoid control against minus one, yielding true when the control is above that threshold.

Architecture helpers classify a register snapshot as user or kernel for sample attribution, fetch the instruction pointer from registers, and expose user register state to tracing filters without transformation.
Guest sample attribution first reads guest state and reports absence when the guest is inactive, otherwise it distinguishes guest user from guest kernel execution.

Event capability predicates test whether branch sampling is requested, whether the backing unit supplies auxiliary recording, whether auxiliary actions or sizing are requested, whether the buffer runs backward, and whether address filtering is available.
Address filter state and asynchronous notification state live only in the parent of a cloned event, so helpers redirect child references to the parent before returning the storage location.

When perf support is compiled out, auxiliary output acquisition yields absence, auxiliary termination does nothing, auxiliary skipping reports an invalid argument, and task migration plus scheduler entry and exit notifications do nothing.

The disabled build makes task initialization, release and pause report success, makes exit, teardown, delayed release, debug printing and scheduler hooks silent no ops, and makes file lookup, attribute lookup, local reading, task disable and enable plus refresh report invalid argument or invalid handle.

The disabled build turns software, breakpoint, mapping, symbol, tracing, execution, identity, namespace, fork, code patching, initialization, period control, enablement and periodic tick notifications into silent no ops with narrow exceptions where recursion acquisition signals absence, period query yields zero, remote disable signals failure and kernel release reports success. Symbol naming is expressed as a callback type accepting a character buffer with length and opaque data.

Period adjustment reports invalid argument while pause reports success and exclusion check reports allowed. Kernel, processor and tracepoint permission helpers grant access when a privileged capability check owned elsewhere succeeds and otherwise deny with access or permission failures.
Debug register restoration and low power notification are empty operations in the fragments shown.

Performance unit sysfs descriptors pair a device attribute with identification and formatting data. The basic form carries a numeric identifier plus an optional event string, the heterogeneous form carries separate strings for threaded modes, the hybrid form adds a unit type alongside identifier and string, and the format form carries only a unit type.
A small output helper forwards a value to a copy routine sized by the value type.

Constructor helpers create read only sysfs entries for events and formats. They cover numeric events with custom display, string events with a common display, single use event identifiers, and format strings that are validated against page size before display.
Processor initialization and teardown hooks for perf are defined as null when the corresponding feature is unavailable.
Branch stack snapshotting is expressed as a callback type that receives an array of branch records.
User register capture state consists of an application binary tag together with a pointer to the underlying register snapshot. A header guard macro records inclusion of these definitions.
Extended register mask support is fixed at zero in both configurations shown.

When register support is unavailable, value reads yield zero, mask validation accepts only an empty mask and otherwise reports unsupported, application interface queries report none, and user state collection uses the current task registers and interface.

Power trace helpers report real time clock validity and enablement when tracing is available and gate device tracing on the enable flag. When unavailable, clock validity always reports true, enablement always reports false, and device, suspend and resume tracing expand to empty loops.

Console switch registration reports success while unregistration does nothing, interconnect memory activity always reports inactive, and the power group name is defined as null. A header guard macro records inclusion of the power definitions.
Power messages carry a single integer event code, exposed under both a structure tag and a typedef alias.

Device power operations form a table of optional callbacks spanning preparation and completion plus early, late and non interruptible variants for suspend, freeze and poweroff images with matching resume paths, alongside runtime suspend, resume and idle handlers.

System sleep, late sleep, non interruptible sleep and runtime groups map paired suspend and resume handlers onto the corresponding table slots, with conditional setters that install the mappings only when power management or sleep support is enabled and otherwise expand to nothing.

Table construction helpers define static operation tables, export them with license and namespace variants, discard them when power management is unavailable, and provide simplified, universal and non interruptible only spellings plus conditional pointer wrappers that yield null when the related configuration is off.

Exhausted callchain storage permanently blocks further plain appends until the context is reset, disabled auxiliary and event paths fail lookups and reads rather than returning data, and permission helpers fail closed when the external capability check is absent.
An external privileged capability check is referenced by permission helpers.
An external error pointer constructor is referenced by disabled lookup helpers.
